rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.err.semXeque: This move gives no check, and Black gains time to bring defenders close to the king.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.err.semXeque.v: Back to the position: the pawn on h7 is defended only by the king. Look for the sacrifice with check.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: with the king castled short, the pawn on h7 is often defended only by the king. The bishop sacrifice on h7 with check is called the Greek gift.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.e2: Game youngopos vs haogou, Lichess. The bishop on d3 aims at h7, the knight on f3 reaches g5, the queen on d1 reaches the h-file, and the pawn on e5 takes the f6 square away from the black knight.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes: the bishop captures the pawn on h7 with check. The three attacking pieces are ready to follow up.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.revela: The sacrifice is the bishop capturing the pawn on h7 with check, to open the black king to the knight and the queen.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.err.f3g5.1: The knight goes to g5 before the sacrifice, without check.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.err.f3g5.2: With this move, the pawn on h7 advances and drives the knight away, and h7 is no longer a target. The advantage is gone.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.err.f3g5.3: Back to the position: the pawn on h7 is defended only by the king. Look for the sacrifice with check.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.fora: That move gives no check. Look for the sacrifice with check on h7.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the sacrifice.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.l.1: The bishop gives itself up with check to remove the pawn that shielded the king.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.l.2: The king captures the bishop. Declining also lost: on h8, the knight and the queen reach the king just the same.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.l.3: The knight gives check on g5, defended by the bishop on c1, and gets out of the queen's way, which now passes through f3.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.l.4: The king goes back to g8. If the queen captured the knight, the bishop on c1 would recapture. On g6 the king would be exposed: the pawn on h2 would advance to h4, threatening check on h5.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.l.5: The queen reaches the h-file and threatens mate on h7, with the knight on g5 guarding that square.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.l.6: Black has no good defence. The queen captures the knight to avoid mate.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.l.7: The bishop recaptures. White gave up the bishop and the knight and won the queen.
rot.bishopSacH7.ideia.ex1.l.8: In positions like this, the Greek gift works with three pieces: the bishop that captures on h7, the knight that reaches g5 and the queen that reaches the h-file.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.laskerBauer.1: Attack: White again. Game Emanuel Lasker vs Johann Bauer, Amsterdam 1889. Here there is no white knight to go to g5. Which piece does its job?
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.laskerBauer.l.1: The bishop gives itself up with check on h7.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.laskerBauer.l.3: The queen captures the knight with check and reaches the h-file without needing the knight.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.laskerBauer.l.4: The king goes back to g8, the only square it has.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.laskerBauer.l.5: The second bishop gives itself up too: it captures the pawn on g7 and strips the king bare.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.laskerBauer.l.6: The king captures the bishop. Without that, the threat was mate with the queen on h8.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.laskerBauer.l.7: The queen gives check along the g-file.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.laskerBauer.l.9: The rook goes to f3, on its way to h3, and threatens mate. To stop it, Bauer had to give up his queen, and Lasker won.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.london.1: Attack: still White. Game OneEyedRaven vs cudevras, Lichess, from a London System. The bishop is on d3, the knight on f3 reaches g5, and the rook on h1 already stands on the open h-file.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.london.l.1: The bishop captures the pawn on h7 with check.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.london.l.3: The knight gives check, and the rook on h1 attacks the knight on h5 along the open file.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.london.l.4: The queen captures the knight. With the king on g8, the white queen would capture on h5 and mate would come soon.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.london.l.5: The bishop recaptures, and White wins the queen for bishop and knight. In positions like this, the rook on the open h-file does the queen's job.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.excecao.1: Attack: still White. Game Donnily_Trampus vs catarino, Lichess. The three pieces of the Greek gift are there, but the black knight on d7 is close to the king.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.excecao.l.3: The knight gives check on g5.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.excecao.l.4: The king goes back to g8.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.excecao.l.5: The queen reaches the h-file and threatens mate on h7.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.excecao.l.6: The knight goes from d7 to f6, guards h7 and attacks the queen. There is no mate, and White is a piece down.
rot.bishopSacH7.demos.excecao.volta: Back to the position: before the sacrifice, check the defenders. Here the knight on d7 could reach f6 and cover h7 in time. In the first position, the pawn on e5 prevented that.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.valeAqui.err.out: After this move Black gains time, and the rook on e8 keeps attacking your back rank. Look for a move with check.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.valeAqui.enuncia: Practice: the bishop on d3 aims at h7 and the queen is already on h5, but there is no knight to go to g5. Does the sacrifice on h7 work here? Check and play as White.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.valeAqui.fim: Yes: the queen captures the rook with check, and Black blocks with the queen on f8. Then the bishop on h7 pulls the king away from guarding f8: here the sacrifice becomes a deflection.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.valeAqui.err.d3h: Without the knight on g5, the king runs to f8, and you lose the bishop. Before the sacrifice, there is a black rook to capture with check.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.valeAqui.err.h5h: The queen gives check on h7, but the king runs to f8, and the attack is over. Look for another move with check.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.classico.enuncia: Still White. The black king is castled, and the pawn on h7 has only the king as a defender. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.classico.fim: The bishop captured on h7 with check and drew the king out. Then the knight gave check on g5 and cleared the way for the queen to reach the h-file.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.classico.err.out: After this move Black gains time to defend the king. Look for the sacrifice with check.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.classico.err.sem: Without check, the king goes back to g8 and the bishop given up is simply lost. The knight on f3 gives check on g5.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.pretas.enunciado: Now let us think from Black's side. The white king is castled, and the pawn on h2 has only the king as a defender. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.pretas.fim: The bishop captured on h2 with check and drew the king out. Then the knight gave check on g4, and the queen and the rook on h8 reach the h-file. It is the same sacrifice, with the colours reversed.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.pretas.err.f6g4: The knight goes to g4 without check, and White gains time to defend h2. The sacrifice comes first.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.pretas.err.outro: After this move White gains time to defend the king. Look for the sacrifice with check.
rot.bishopSacH7.pratica.pretas.err.semXe: Without check, the white king goes back to g1 and the bishop given up is simply lost. The knight on f6 gives check on g4.
